idea: Split the list in half, sort each half the same way, then merge the two sorted halves by repeatedly taking the smaller front element. Splitting costs nothing; the work is in the merging.
useWhen: You need a guaranteed O(n log n) time
Sorting linked lists or data that does not fit in memory
The order of equal items must stay as it was (it is stable)
avoidWhen: Memory is tight: it needs extra space for the merge
The list is tiny: a simple insertion sort is quicker in practice
